turns.question: Can you check 75 km around EBTL? Are any Indian cobra records within 10 km of elephant records?
turns.answer:
Using public data only, I treated EBTL as its public Budhimutlu location in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu: about `12.70735, 78.18994` from the EBTL site address and Budhimutlu map listing. Sources: [EBTL site](https://ebtl.earth/cegs/), [Mapcarta Budhimutlu](https://mapcarta.com/35028154).

What I found:
- `Found`: public Indian cobra records within 75 km of EBTL.
- One clear record is at `Post Box no 4, Haritha, Amritha, Hosur` with coordinates `12.7394, 77.7867`, about `44 km` from EBTL. Source: [India Biodiversity Portal cobra record](https://indiabiodiversity.org/observation/show/17993858).
- Another cobra locality is `MQF9+X4G, Sundaram garden area, Belagondanahalli` with coordinates `12.6760, 77.7674`, about `46 km` from EBTL. Source: [India Biodiversity Portal place page with coordinates](https://thewesternghats.indiabiodiversity.org/observation/show/18738185), plus [iNaturalist checklist showing Indian cobra there](https://www.inaturalist.org/lists/4379541).

On the elephant question:
- `Found`: strong public evidence that elephants occur in the wider Hosur-Melagiri landscape. Sources: [BNHS article on Hosur and Dharmapuri elephant status](https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/395224), [Melagiri overview](https://indiabiodiversity.org/group/melagiri/page/30), [Tamil Nadu Forest Dept Yaanai site](https://www.tnfdyaanai.com/).
- `Not found`: a public elephant point record with open coordinates close enough for me to test the `10 km` rule against the cobra points.

Answer:
- I can confirm `Indian cobra records exist within 75 km of EBTL`.
- I `cannot confirm any cobra record within 10 km of an elephant record` from public, open-coordinate records alone.
- This is `not the same as saying no`; it means the needed public elephant point records were missing or obscured.

What is missing:
- exact EBTL project coordinates, beyond the public Budhimutlu address
- open-coordinate elephant occurrence records in the same area
- any private project sightings or raw exports you may already have

If you want, I can next turn this into a simple table: `species | place | coordinates | distance from EBTL | source`.

turns.question: So does that mean cobras and elephants were in the same place at the same time?
turns.answer:
No.

What I found:
- Public records show `Indian cobra` in the wider EBTL area.
- Public sources also show `elephants` in the wider Hosur-Melagiri landscape.

What I did not find:
- A public pair of records showing `cobra and elephant at the same place and the same time`.
- A public elephant point record close enough to the cobra records to confirm the `within 10 km` part.

So the safe answer is:
- `We cannot say yes from public data.`
- `We also cannot prove no.`

This means:
- `Same general landscape`: yes, likely.
- `Same exact place at the same time`: not confirmed.

Sources used:
- EBTL public location: [EBTL site](https://ebtl.earth/cegs/)
- Cobra records: [India Biodiversity Portal](https://indiabiodiversity.org/observation/show/17993858), [Western Ghats / India Biodiversity record](https://thewesternghats.indiabiodiversity.org/observation/show/18738185)
- Elephant landscape presence: [BNHS article](https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/395224), [Melagiri page](https://indiabiodiversity.org/group/melagiri/page/30), [TN Forest Dept Yaanai](https://www.tnfdyaanai.com/)

What is missing:
- Open, exact elephant occurrence coordinates and dates near EBTL
- Any project camera trap, patrol, or sighting data

turns.question: What information do we need to know that properly?
turns.answer:
To know that properly, we need `record-level data` for both species, not just general area information.

What we need:
- `Exact location` for each cobra record and each elephant record, preferably GPS coordinates
- `Exact date and time` for each record
- `A clear distance rule`, such as “within 10 km”
- `A clear time rule`, such as “same day”, “within 24 hours”, or “same week”
- `Reliable species ID` for both records
- `Source details` for each record, such as camera trap, field sighting, rescue log, or public biodiversity record

Then we can test:
- `Place`: are any cobra and elephant records within 10 km?
- `Time`: do those nearby records happen in the same time window?

What I found:
- Public sources show cobras in the wider EBTL area.
- Public sources show elephants in the wider Hosur-Melagiri landscape.

What is missing:
- Open elephant point records near EBTL with usable coordinates and dates
- A defined time window for “same time”
- Any project records that may exist but are not public

Public sources used:
- [EBTL site](https://ebtl.earth/cegs/)
- [India Biodiversity Portal cobra record](https://indiabiodiversity.org/observation/show/17993858)
- [Western Ghats / India Biodiversity cobra-related record](https://thewesternghats.indiabiodiversity.org/observation/show/18738185)
- [BNHS article on elephants in Hosur-Dharmapuri landscape](https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/395224)
- [Melagiri landscape page](https://indiabiodiversity.org/group/melagiri/page/30)
- [TN Forest Dept Yaanai](https://www.tnfdyaanai.com/)

Short version: we need `exact coordinates`, `exact dates/times`, and a `defined time window` to answer it correctly.
